content.title: Flex Direction and Gap
content.hook: A flex container can arrange items in a row or a column.
content.context: The property that chooses the main direction is `flex-direction`.
goals: Control the main direction of a flex layout and use `gap` for consistent space between flex items.

content.title: Row versus column

content.question: What is the most likely visible change when a flex container changes from row to column?

options.text: Its direct children move from a horizontal arrangement to a vertical arrangement.
The parent stops being a flex container.

feedback.correct: `flex-direction` changes the direction in which the flex items are arranged.
feedback.incorrect: `flex-direction` changes the direction in which the flex items are arranged.

content.title: Gap

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
Build a three-item toolbar.

First use row.

Then switch to column.

Finally add `gap: 12px` and observe how the relationship stays consistent.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.
content.sampleResponse: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.

feedback.correct: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.
feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.question:
You add a fourth item.

With `gap: 12px`, what should you expect?

options.text: The browser continues applying the same gap between flex items.
Only the first three items receive space.
The new item replaces the first item.

feedback.correct: `gap` belongs to the relationship among the flex items, so a newly added item participates in that same spacing rule.
feedback.incorrect: `gap` belongs to the relationship among the flex items, so a newly added item participates in that same spacing rule.

content.question: Which rule best expresses “these controls are stacked with consistent space”?

feedback.correct: The answer directly describes the layout relationship: column direction plus consistent space between siblings.
feedback.incorrect: The answer directly describes the layout relationship: column direction plus consistent space between siblings.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Direction chooses the main axis; gap describes space between flex items.
**Senior habit:** Prefer one rule that expresses a relationship over a pile of one-off nudges.
**Mastery signal:** You can switch a flex layout from row to column and predict what changes before you refresh the page.
